feature_units: mm (NASA POWER PRECTOTCORR daily precipitation; 24h = latest daily value, 72h = sum of last 3 daily values, 7d = sum over the fetch window)

training_data.description: Positive examples (label=1): real landslide events from NASA's Global Landslide Catalog (GLC), filtered to India, each paired with real cumulative rainfall (rain_24h/72h/7d) from the NASA POWER API for the days leading up to the event. Negative examples (label=0): the same real locations, on random non-event dates (2015-2026), with real rainfall from NASA POWER for those dates.
training_data.caveat: Rainfall-only model (3 features: rain_24h, rain_72h, rain_7d). Real landslides also depend on slope, soil saturation, geology, and land cover, none of which are inputs to this classifier, so its predict_proba output should be read as 'how closely does this rainfall pattern resemble rainfall that historically preceded a landslide in this region', not a calibrated physical probability. Combine with this project's separate slope_saturation_index (backend/app/services/slope_stability.py) for a fuller risk picture - do not treat this model's output alone as a complete hazard assessment.

evaluation.method: 80/20 train/test split (stratified), random_state=42, evaluated once on the held-out 20%
evaluation.notes: Recall on the landslide class (0.83) is higher than on no-landslide (0.70) - the model is biased toward flagging risk rather than missing it, which is the right trade-off for an early-warning system (a false alarm is cheaper than a missed landslide). The roughly-equal feature importances indicate the model uses short-term and cumulative rainfall together rather than relying on a single window.
